Basic Parts of the Cell
Plasma Membrane: cell’s outer boundary
Cover’s the cell’s surface and acts as a barrier
Materials enterand exitthrough plasma membrane
Cytoplasm: region of the cell within the plasma membrane
Includes fluid, cytoskeleton, and all organellesexcept nucleus
Cytosol: part of cytoplasm that includes molecules, small particles (i.e. ribosomes)
Composed of ~20% protein
Control Center: membrane-bound organelle that contains the cellular DNA (nucleus)
Controlsmost functionsof the cell
Largest cell structure; easiest to see
Maintains its shape via protein skeleton known as nuclear matrix
explanation: All cells share three basic parts. The plasma membrane is the outer boundary that covers the cell's surface and acts as a selective barrier through which materials enter and exit. The cytoplasm is the entire region within the plasma membrane, which includes the fluid, cytoskeleton, and all organelles except the nucleus. The cytosol is the fluid portion of the cytoplasm, containing molecules and small particles (like ribosomes) and is composed of about 20% protein. The control center is the membrane-bound organelle that contains DNA, known as the nucleus; it controls most cellular functions, is the largest and easiest cell structure to see, and maintains its shape using a protein skeleton called the nuclear matrix.

questions.q: Which part of the cell is described as the fluid portion of the cytoplasm, containing ribosomes and being composed of approximately 20% protein?
questions.exp: The cytosol is defined as the part of the cytoplasm including molecules and small particles like ribosomes, and is composed of ~20% protein.

questions.q: What protein skeleton maintains the shape of the nucleus (control center)?
questions.exp: The slide states that the nucleus maintains its shape via a protein skeleton known as the nuclear matrix.
